milestone: M12 External Mode Pack Execution Policy

strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Direct external active Mode Pack tasks are now bound to the runtime-owned active snapshot identity captured at task.start and revalidated at task.run.
Rust denies stale active Mode Pack snapshot, missing mode, malformed provenance, or policy fingerprint mismatch before TaskRunning or side effects.
Headless callers can resume delayed external Mode Pack tasks without reconstructing active policy state or trusting stale caller-side evidence.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances mode_pack_runtime with supporting runtime_permission_enforcement, persistent_structured_ledger, and headless_autonomous_development.
answers.new_capability: A task started under an active external Mode Pack can run only when the current active snapshot source, activation fingerprint, mode, and policy fingerprint still match the bounded task-start provenance.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: M21.1 revalidated live workspace Mode Pack files, but active replacement and rollback can change runtime-owned active snapshots without a live-file provenance model being sufficient.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: A delayed external active Mode Pack task can be admitted under one active policy and later run after replacement or rollback without a point-of-use active-snapshot denial.
answers.non_duplicative: Distinct from M56.4 apply, M56.5 verification, and M56.6 objective acceptance, and also distinct from M12.1 handoff target admission, M12.2 child provenance, M12.3 initial activation, and M21.1 live-file revalidation.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The implementation extends existing task.start provenance and task.run admission; it adds no JSON-RPC method.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. It adds no report, digest, history, readiness, verdict, preview, dashboard, or inspection surface.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: task.run compares captured external Mode Pack task provenance against the current active snapshot including source kind, source token, policy fingerprint, and activation fingerprint before TaskRunning.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Controllers can safely run or reject external Mode Pack tasks after long delays using bounded runtime evidence instead of re-reading raw Mode Pack files.
answers.milestone_progress: Closes the direct active-snapshot execution-policy gap after local activation, active replacement, rollback, and remote candidate lifecycle work.

exit_criteria: task.start records bounded external_modepack_task_provenance with active snapshot source kind, source token, policy fingerprint, and activation fingerprint when an external mode resolves from active Mode Pack state
task.run accepts matching active external Mode Pack provenance and proceeds through the existing task execution path
task.run denies stale active snapshot, missing mode, malformed provenance, replacement, rollback, or activation/policy fingerprint mismatch before TaskRunning

denial evidence is duplicate-safe on replay and excludes raw Mode Pack JSON, prompts, provider responses, file content, commands, outputs, environment values, absolute paths, canonical paths, and secrets
built-in mode tasks and existing live-workspace external Mode Pack revalidation continue to pass
behavior_evidence: Rust tests cover active external Mode Pack task.run success for a remote active candidate snapshot
Rust tests cover stale active snapshot denial after active remote replacement before TaskRunning
Existing Rust tests continue to cover live workspace Mode Pack deletion/change/malformed denial and built-in mode compatibility

non_goals: no Mode Pack fetch, approval, replacement, rollback, or route-drive expansion
